narrative:
The model estimates a 73% chance that you will leave your job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This prediction is driven primarily by three key aspects of your profile that strongly signal higher turnover risk compared to employees expected to stay.

Your total years of professional experience stands out as the most influential factor. At 6-10 years, you fall into a mid-career stage where many employees begin exploring new opportunities, pushing the prediction noticeably toward leaving. Second, the fact that you have received other job offers while at your current company adds substantial weight toward departure, as external opportunities often indicate readiness to move on. Third, having spent only 1-5 years in your present role—typical of relatively recent arrivals—further increases the likelihood of leaving, since shorter tenure in the current organization frequently correlates with lower attachment.

These three elements together outweigh many positive signals in your profile, such as high job support, strong emotional commitment, recognition from superiors, and satisfaction with your work environment. Because the model sees your experience level, external opportunities, and shorter current tenure as the dominant drivers, it concludes you are more likely to leave than to remain long-term.

The organization should discuss retention strategies with you, such as clearer promotion paths or expanded responsibilities. You may wish to reflect on whether your external opportunities better align with your career goals. Addressing these factors openly could still change the outlook. (248 words)
